name: Screen Grotesque
description: Inter, self-hosted with its optical sizes, for every role but code: the sharper Inter Display cut at heading sizes over its even text cut, with a system monospace for code.

provenance.attribution: Inter, by The Inter Project Authors, self-hosted from Fontsource's npm package for the keyurgolani.name portfolio platform.
provenance.maintainer: The upstream projects, at the versions fonts.provenance.json pins
provenance.derivation: Role metrics by the platform for the aurora-glass and flux direction (packs-plan §3.2), with display and headline tracking eased for Inter Display's tighter cut; font files, the wght and opsz variable subsets, copied unmodified from @fontsource-variable/inter 5.3.0.

fallbacks: Inter is followed by metric-matched fallback faces over local system fonts (size-adjust and ascent, descent, and line-gap overrides), then a system stack and a generic family.
There's a fallback face at each weight the roles set, over the system bold for a heading, each sized to Inter at that weight and its role's optical size.
Glyphs outside every shipped face's unicode-range render in the declared system stack, so text never goes missing.
caveats: Code is the system monospace: the pack ships no mono face.
Inter ships upright only: em in running text renders as a slanted Inter, since its italic would take the faces a Latin page loads past 102,400 B.
Inter's latin-ext subset (133,336 B) loads only on a page whose text needs it, such as ő or ł; a Latin page loads 72,920 B. Other scripts render in the declared system stack.

A fallback face at one weight serves every role at that weight, measured at the largest optical size among them, so a smaller role at that weight (label, caption, numeric) falls back a few percent narrow.
